story.head: The Oilers are on a heater
paras: The Oilers won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in overtime in Edmonton on Wednesday. The Flyers (6-10-6) beat Columbus 4-3 last night, and the Oilers have won four straight. Going in, the Oilers are first in the Pacific (third in the NHL) and the Flyers sixth in the Metropolitan (tied for 26th).
The Oilers’ record (.786) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.577), largely thanks to their finishing. The Flyers’ record (.409) is about what their chances are worth.

The Oilers ice the puck less than almost anyone (3rd) and have a dangerous power play (3rd). They also lean hard on their top players (lowest), so the Flyers roll four lines, but them lean on their top six. Edmonton has scored 3.86 goals a game, the third most in the league. The Flyers take away shots from the point (4th lowest) and get a lot of their shots blocked (31st). Philadelphia has scored 2.32 goals a game, the second fewest in the league. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, especially the Flyers (2nd lowest), so expect a tight one.

Connor McDavid (11 G / 39 A / 50 P in 21 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with ten points in his last five games. Leon Draisaitl (18 G / 20 A / 38 P in 21 GP) has a team-high 18 goals, the most in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games. For the Flyers, Matvei Michkov (11 G / 5 A / 16 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in five straight games against Edmonton. Trevor Zegras (5 G / 10 A / 15 P in 22 GP) isn’t far behind.
Tristan Jarry (5-1-3 / .903 SV% in 9 GS) is expected to start for Edmonton, and Dan Vladař (3-4-4 / .879 SV% in 11 GS) for Philadelphia.
